explanation: Singapore's hawker and noodle-dish culture (influenced heavily by Chinese and Malay food traditions) is informal, and no etiquette source specifically flags slurping noodles as rude. It isn't treated as a special compliment to the cook the way it is in Japan, but it isn't a breach of manners either, especially at hawker centres.
local_tip: Eat noodle soups however feels natural at a hawker centre - nobody will bat an eye at a bit of noise; just dial it back in a quiet, upscale restaurant.

also_check.note: Slurping noodles is a genuine compliment to the chef and considered normal, even in nicer restaurants.
Audible slurping is generally seen as poor table manners, especially outside very casual settings.
Slurping pasta or any food is seen as a clear breach of table manners.

sources.title: Etiquette in Singapore - Frommer's (chopstick/noodle dining customs)
